section.title: Write to expose the gaps in your thinking
section.deck: Leslie Lamport explains how hierarchical proofs make hidden reasoning steps visible.

blocks.question: Why does writing help us think?
answer: Lamport begins with the ease of fooling oneself. While proving increasingly complicated concurrent algorithms correct, he found that his usual mathematical proof style made it hard to track every detail and check whether each obligation had been satisfied. A convincing overall impression did not give him a reliable way to account for all the steps.

His response was hierarchical structure. A proof consists of steps; each step has its own justification, either a paragraph or another sequence of smaller justified steps. The writer identifies which earlier facts support a particular conclusion. If the conclusion does not follow from those facts, the proof is wrong even if the theorem itself happens to be true. Breaking the argument into layers makes those gaps inspectable.

Lamport says the approach worked for proofs of programs and then for ordinary mathematical theorems. He also recalls an unexpectedly angry response when presenting it to a small group of mathematicians. He interprets their reaction as fear that they would have to write proofs for a computer program. That interpretation is his account of the experience, rather than evidence of what every participant actually believed.

He stresses that hierarchical organization does not automatically demand more formal notation. The change is to organize the argument and identify the facts each step uses. It does create more work when it reveals things the author has not actually stated: what felt obvious in thought may turn out to be a missing step on paper. Writing therefore tests whether apparent understanding survives a clear explanation.

blocks.title: Make an argument inspectable

steps.title: State the conclusion
steps.text: Write down what you believe is true.

steps.title: Name its dependencies
steps.text: Identify the facts the step relies on.

steps.title: Inspect the gaps
steps.text: Check that the conclusion follows from those facts.
